intro.task: Write an SML configuration that includes name (string gateway), port (integer 8080), debug (boolean true), tags (array containing logging and metrics). After finishing writing, click on 'Verify' and then look at the parsing results.
intro.main:
name: gateway
port: 8080
debug: true
tags: [ logging metrics ]
intro.hint: Try changing the port to "8080" (in quotation marks), and the verification will tell you that it is not an integer 8080.

ch01.task: Describe a person using SML: firstName("John Doe"), state(Naked words NY), age(27), ratio(0.75), enabled(true), note(null). Pay attention to when quotation marks must be added.
ch01.main:
firstName: "John Doe"
state: NY
age: 27
ratio: 0.75
enabled: true
note: null
chinese: 中文无需引号
ch01.hint: Remove the quotation marks from firstName and see if the naked word NY and the quotation mark string "John Doe" are both strings in the result - the answer is: they are both strings, but NY does not need quotation marks.

ch02.task: Write an address block (street, city="New York", state=NY), an database block containing two primary/duplicate sub blocks (each containing host and port=5432), and an users array with elements containing name/role blocks.
ch02.hint: Try writing address { } as address: { }, will the result be the same?

ch03.task: Define @base { region, timeout }, and then write two service blocks (auth, billing) both &base, each covering port and name.
ch03.hint: Miswrite&base as the naked word (remove&) and see what happens.

ch04.task: include "ui" as ui， Among them, ui.sml has title and powered. The main file is accessed through ui.title/ui.powered.
ch04.main:
include "ui" as ui
title: ui.title
powered: ui.powered
ch04.hint: Add an second.sml file and include "second" as s in the main file to access s.xxx.

ch05.task: Define @contract Server strict { name: str, port: int min 1024 max 65535, region: str }, and write a valid data using @is Server (name=lobby, port=25565, region=ap-est-1).
ch05.hint: Change the port to 80 (less than 1024) and see how the contract validation reports an error.

ch06.task: Write an secrets block, including apiKey: $env.RESEND_API_KEY and dbPassword: $env.DB_PASSWORD; Write another banner string using \u{1F680} to escape emojis.
ch06.hint: It is not possible to set real environment variables in the browser, so $env.X will parse as an empty string - this is the expected behavior, and validation will determine based on this.

ch07.task: Define @contract User { id: str, email: str, role: enum(user,admin,owner) default user }, write data using @is User (id=u_1, email=a @ b.c), and verify that the role automatically takes the default user.
ch07.hint: The same contract behaves consistently in Rust/C/JS/Lua - try changing role to owner.

ch08.task: Write a deployment configuration that is close to reality: @contract Service Defined in the main file, @is Service write name/port/debug; Service auth and billing are both &base and cover port/name; The database block contains url($env) and pool{min,max}; Features array.
ch08.hint: This is a deployment configuration that is close to reality: contract+fragment+$env used together (contract definition is placed in the main file to avoid cross file references).

ch09.task: Using contract combination: Define @contract Endpoint { host: str, port: int } and @contract Service { name: str, main: Endpoint, peers: array[Endpoint] ? }, and then use @is Service to write the main and a peers element.
ch09.hint: Endpoint is reused by the main field and array[Endpoint], which is called 'contract combination'.

ch10.task: Use include to load multiple subfiles into their respective namespaces: include "auth.sml" as auth and include "billing.sml" as billing. Each subfile uses @is Module and includes a name field. Verify that both the auth and billing namespaces are correctly loaded.
ch10.main:
include "auth.sml" as auth
include "billing.sml" as billing
root: ok
ch10.hint: Include... as auth/as billing loads different files into isolated namespaces to avoid field conflicts.

appendix.task: Write a SML: name(John), age(27), adesk block with city=NY, tags, array length 2. This paragraph should yield consistent results in any language parsing.
appendix.main:
name: John
age: 27
address: { city: NY }
tags: [ a b ]
appendix.hint: Imagine this paragraph as Rust/C/JS/Lua parsing, where the field names and nested structures should be exactly the same.
